{{Short description|British and Irish mathematician (1866–1934)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=January 2022}}
{{EngvarB|date=January 2022}}
[[file:W M Orr.jpg|thumb|right|250px]]

'''William McFadden Orr''', [[Fellow of the Royal Society|FRS]]<ref name="frs">{{Cite journal | last1 = Conway | first1 = A. W. | title = William McFadden Orr. 1866-1934 | doi = 10.1098/rsbm.1935.0019 | journal = [[Obituary Notices of Fellows of the Royal Society]] | volume = 1 | issue = 4 | pages = 559–562 | year = 1935 | jstor = 768986| doi-access = free }}</ref> (2 May 1866 &ndash; 14 August 1934) was a British and Irish [[mathematician]].

He was born in [[Comber]], [[County Down]] and educated at [[Methodist College Belfast]] and [[Queen's College, Belfast]] under [[John Purser (mathematician)|John Purser]], before entering [[St John's College, Cambridge]] and graduating as [[Senior Wrangler]] in 1888.<ref>{{acad|id=OR885WM|name=Orr, William McFadden}}</ref>  He was elected a fellow of his college, and became a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] in 1909.<ref name="frs"/>

He was appointed professor of mathematics at the [[Royal College of Science for Ireland]] in 1892 and professor of [[pure mathematics]] and [[applied mathematics]] when the college merged with [[University College Dublin]] in 1926.  He retired in 1933 and died in 1934.<ref name="frs"/>

[[Orr–Sommerfeld equation]] in [[fluid dynamics]] is named after his work in 1907.<ref>* {{Cite journal |last=Orr |first=W. M'F. |author-link=William McFadden Orr |year=1907 |title=The stability or instability of the steady motions of a liquid. Part I |journal=Proceedings of the Royal Irish Academy |volume=27 |pages=9–68}}
* {{Cite journal |last=Orr |first=W. M'F. |author-link=William McFadden Orr |year=1907 |title=The stability or instability of the steady motions of a liquid. Part II |journal=Proceedings of the Royal Irish Academy |volume=27 |pages=69–138}}</ref>
